adjudication_summary: Source-reviewed re-review repaired the missing activity layer and database reconciliation for doi__10.1002_pro.5088. The paper is publication-grade with cautions: primary activity/toxicity rows are complete from Supplementary Table S1, database endpoint-label conflicts are preserved, and mechanism evidence is limited to phenotype/no-direct-mechanism framing.

caution_findings.note: Worker-4 preserved 18 database-vs-primary-source conflicts: MBIC labels where primary Table S1 reports MBC, a DeNo1009 MBIC/lost-greater-than mismatch, and comparator/value differences such as database >128 versus primary >=128. These conflicts do not block publication-grade review because the primary Table S1 rows are present and the database rows are explicitly labeled source_conflict.
The packet linked assay rows cover 41 of 58 peptide names, while worker-2 extracted primary-source activity/toxicity rows for all 58 selected peptides from Supplementary Table S1.

The paper supports antimicrobial/hemolysis phenotypes and AMP background rationale, but no direct mechanism assay for the generated peptides; final mechanism layer explicitly prevents direct-mechanism promotion.

The packet still records material_extracted_with_gaps from the framework test, but the blocking analysis gaps were closed by reopening XML, PDF text, supplementary PDF text, OA package members, and database snapshots.
